title: Hello, with a system call
description:
Print a two-line greeting with one `write` system call and exit with code 0.

```
Hello from assembly!
Registers: rax, rdi, rsi, rdx
```

starter.main.asm:
global  _start

        section .data
msg:    db      "Hello from assembly!", 10

        section .text
_start:
        ; TODO: write(1, msg, length)

        mov     eax, 60
        xor     edi, edi
        syscall

hints: `msg_len equ $ - msg` right after the data gives the number of bytes from `msg` to that point (lesson 1.05).
`write` is system call 1: `rax` = 1, `rdi` = 1 (standard output), `rsi` = the address, `rdx` = the length (lesson 1.04).
requirements: Both lines are one block of `db` data with `10` for each new line.
Work out the length with `equ $ - label`, not by counting.
Name the system call numbers with `equ`.
stretch: Print the same text twice by putting the `write` in a block you jump back to once (milestone 3 covers jumps).
